results.name: an identical memory in the same folder is recognised instead of filed twice
duplicate recognition is opt-in: a deliberate re-save still produces a second memory
recognition is by decoded bytes and is confined to one folder
a trashed memory does not block saving it again
an unreadable neighbour cannot break or fake duplicate recognition
onDuplicate is validated, and an invalid value writes nothing
grouping sends the same bytes to the folder the human chose, and cannot escape the Recall root
a save outside the Recall root is refused whatever the grouping asked for
memories are never written into Persistent Storage, and the archive says so plainly
the exclusions that exist are real: query tokens are dropped and a declared label cannot smuggle them back
deleting a memory removes the pair together and restoring brings the pair back
a memory cannot be half-deleted through the pair endpoint
only the refetch method may claim the bytes came from the URL it names
